7ec3bfd5961514ab94176a4074863389a8bbd31d
Defer PostgreSQL socket I/O from the poll scan into session handlers

The phased scheduler previously read, decrypted and framed every ready
frontend request in ProcessAllMyDS_AfterPoll before any session could
submit a query or consume a backend completion. This imposed a batch
barrier even when connection starvation made backend response processing
and immediate reuse the useful next work.

Give PgSQL_Thread a readiness-only after-poll scan. It records events on
the owning data stream and marks the session runnable. Notification-pipe
reads and listener accepts run through a separate housekeeping path,
because those descriptors have no normal session handler. The MySQL scan
and scheduling algorithm are unchanged.

Move the existing data-stream read/TLS/framing/error path behind
consume_data_stream_readiness, called at the beginning of the PostgreSQL
session handler. Preserve idle-backend notification and failure checks
before frontend parsing can change session state, including pinned
backends other than the current one. Native query-response processing
continues through the existing backend protocol handler.

Store readiness independently of poll-array indices: waiter rearm cleanup
can remove a stream from the poll set before its handler runs. Consume
pending events once and clear them on backend attach/detach. Give parked
waiters an I/O-only handler invocation for periodic frontend checks, so
a disconnected waiting client can be detected without an empty-pool retry.

Retain the phased early-dispatch and inline connection-handoff behavior.
The intended benefit is earlier useful backend work interleaved with
frontend I/O, not elimination of the CPU cost of reading requests.

Validation at this checkpoint: release build with PROXYSQL31=1, -O2 and
frame pointers; git diff --check. Focused runtime and performance results
will be recorded in a separate commit. No repository tests were changed.

b17a986f384c55a14ef7f3349a01d37f23f87be8
Drain deferred socket events while PostgreSQL query execution is paused

Review found that moving frontend reads into handler() exposed a scheduling
gap: normal handler calls are gated by pause_until, but frontend POLLIN
remains armed during a query delay. Unread input or EOF could therefore
keep poll immediately runnable until the delay expired and postpone client
disconnect cleanup.

Use the I/O-only handler path for runnable paused sessions as well as
parked pool waiters. It consumes pending frontend and all pinned-backend
events without advancing the query state machine or retrying a checkout.
Retain health and killed-session guards and the normal cleanup path.
Apply the same rule at the optional unified scheduler's ready-dispatch
pause gate, leaving its waiter-enqueue loop free of session mutations.

Validation: independent review confirmed the final placement and ownership
semantics; release rebuild with PROXYSQL31=1 and git diff --check passed.
The focused runtime harness will additionally check disconnect cleanup
inside a five-second query delay before measuring the unchanged 50-client,
64-backend TLS workload. No repository tests were modified.
